title: ENG-205 Sir Gawain Part 3 — 3 Numbers & Dates
subject: ENG-205

cards.term: New Year's Day at the Green Chapel
cards.def: Night passes and New Year draws near; Gawain rises before dawn, keeps the appointment, and the Green Knight says that with New Year come Gawain is called to account.
The Green Knight raises the axe three times: first a feint when Gawain flinches, second a withheld stroke when Gawain stands still, and third the nick that draws blood.
The first blow is stopped after Gawain shrinks at the shoulders, and the Green Knight goads that this is not the Gawain who never blinked when his own head flew.
The second launch leaves Gawain untouched because he stands stone-still like a tree stump, matching the morning he kissed Bertilak's wife then kindly kissed Bertilak.

cards.term: Third swing = nick for the girdle
cards.def: The third blow skews aside, skims the skin, and snicks the flesh because the third time Gawain strayed by keeping the belt, so he feels the blade therefore.
After the nick the Green Knight says one strike was promised—consider yourself well paid—and from any lingering loyalties Gawain is hereby released.
The Green Knight reminds Gawain that twelvemonths ago at this time Gawain took what was his, so the return blow is now due.
The guide claims the wildman is more powerful than any person alive and four times the figure of any fighting knight in Arthur's house, Hector, or any other hero.
The Green Knight whirls into view with a Danish-style axe whose shining lace marks a blade at least four foot long, filed on a stone.
Seeing his blood on the snow, Gawain leaps forward a spear's length at least, rams on his helmet, and brandishes his sword to end the game.
Before leaving the castle Gawain bound himself twice about with the lady's lace girdle, wearing it to save his skin rather than for beauty.
Arthur's whole court agrees that every knight of the Table should bear such a bright green belt worn obliquely to the body, crosswise like a sash, for Gawain's sake.
